findings.rule: Make every "the X" and "its" point to something named in the current or previous sentence.
findings.input:
Under CI the tool freezes the lock by default, and the lock's hashes do not pin (#57),
  # so the flag makes a stamp in CI do what a stamp elsewhere does.
findings.finding: The comment block says "the tool" and "the flag", but neither the comment nor the sentence before names `skills` or `--no-frozen-lockfile`, so the reader has to work out both from the command line under it.

findings.rule: Give one thing one name throughout a text, and never use that name for a second thing.
findings.input: an upstream release must not change every stamp overnight. ... so the flag makes a stamp in CI do what a stamp elsewhere does.
findings.finding: In this comment block "stamp" means two things: the stamped output that an upstream release changes, and the install run in CI, while the glossary defines stamp as the verb "to instantiate".

findings.rule: Keep each fact in one place and reference it from everywhere else, and let a declared copy name its source and update path.
findings.input:
"""A stamp in CI does what a stamp elsewhere does: restore every skill and refresh the lock.
    A fixed version keeps an upstream release from changing every stamp overnight."""
findings.finding: The docstring repeats the rationale in the copier.yml task comment almost word for word, so the two will drift apart once one of them is edited.

findings.rule: Keep each fact in one place and reference it from everywhere else, and let a declared copy name its source and update path.
findings.input: a post-render step runs `npx skills@1.7.6 experimental_install --no-frozen-lockfile` to populate `.agents/skills/`
findings.finding: The Skills list item copies the exact pinned version from copier.yml without naming it as a copy, and the new test accepts any version, so bumping the pin leaves the README stale and nothing catches it.
